definitions.explanation: Describes something striking in scale, force, or degree — so much so that it is almost overwhelming. Can be positive or negative depending on context.

examples.japanese: {物凄|ものすご}い{人|ひと}{出|で}だ。
{外|そと}は{物凄|ものすご}い{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている。
{彼|かれ}は{物凄|ものすご}いスピードで{仕事|しごと}を{片|かた}づけていった。
examples.english: He cleared through the work at an incredible speed.

notes:
An intensifying adjective stressing great scale or degree. Frequently written in hiragana (ものすごい). The adverbial {物凄|ものすご}く is extremely common as a casual intensifier meaning 'very'.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物凄|ものすご}い{勢|いきお}い: tremendous momentum
- {物凄|ものすご}く{暑|あつ}い: incredibly hot
- {物凄|ものすご}い{数|かず}: a huge number

SIMILAR WORDS:
- すごい: amazing; great — milder and more everyday; ものすごい is a stronger intensification

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {物凄|ものすご}くなかったら
